# Bicycle (`bicycle`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/navigation.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Navigation, transport & exploration (`navigation`)
- Deps: helped by ball_bearings, rubber_vulcanisation, bessemer_steel, gears_gear_trains
- Core idea: A two-wheeled frame stays up because the rider steers into any lean, much as one balances a stick on a finger; the forward-raked fork makes the front wheel partly self-steering. The modern safety bicycle has two equal wheels, a chain drive to the rear wheel with a larger front sprocket, a diamond frame of steel tube and air-filled tyres. Even Drais's wooden running machine without pedals (1817) ran 13–15 km/h.
- Pitfalls:
  - Citing Leonardo's 'bicycle' sketch from the Codex Atlanticus; it is generally considered a modern addition (published 1974, contested since)
  - Thinking balance needs speed alone or gyroscopes; steering geometry and rider correction matter most
  - Direct-drive front wheels without gearing: the wheel has to be huge (penny-farthing) and dangerous
- History: europe: 1817 – Drais's running machine, Mannheim; 1860s pedal velocipede in Paris (Michaux, Lallement); 1870s high-wheeler; 1885 Starley's Rover safety bicycle; 1888 Dunlop's pneumatic tyre
- Read:
  - David V. Herlihy, Bicycle: The History (2004)
